architecture.tabModel: One global workspace tab strip. Every browser page, file, PDF, spreadsheet, Terminal, Files, Git, Usage, and Notes surface is a peer tab; there is no nested browser tab strip.

browserResidency.policy: true LRU with the active page protected; evicted pages retain bounded resume metadata and remount on user or agent activation

architecture.manualProcessObservation: A packaged two-cycle churn run created and closed 30 disposable browser peers. Metadata reached the hard cap of 30, a 31st creation was rejected, and both peaks retained exactly six guest renderers. Both cleanups returned to the four-renderer baseline; final browser-core RSS was 0.9% above baseline, no disposable tab restored after restart, and no helper survived quit.

tests.title: Packaged browser churn, caps, cleanup, and restart
evidence: Computer Use created 20 independent browser peer tabs from a 10-tab baseline, reaching the 30-tab metadata ceiling in the sole global workspace strip.
A 31st Cmd+T produced no additional tab and the packaged main-process log reported the expected Browser tab limit reached (30) rejection.
The first peak used six guest renderer processes; closing only the 20 disposable peers returned immediately to the four-renderer baseline and preserved the original 10 tab titles in order.
A second cycle created and closed 10 more peers; its peak again used six guest renderers and cleanup again returned to four.
Final browser-core RSS was 855,872 KiB versus an 848,416 KiB baseline, a 7,456 KiB or 0.9% delta. Main-process RSS finished 12.1% below baseline.
After clean quit, zero packaged Y Space or helper processes remained. Relaunch restored exactly the original 10 tabs and none of the 30 disposable tabs.
